questions.question: How do ItemReader, ItemProcessor, and ItemWriter work together in Spring Batch chunk processing?
questions.title: ItemReader, ItemProcessor, and ItemWriter: Chunk Processing in Spring Batch
questions.direct_answer: In chunk-oriented processing, **`ItemReader`** reads one item at a time until the chunk size is reached, **`ItemProcessor`** optionally transforms or filters each item (returning `null` to skip), and **`ItemWriter`** receives the entire chunk as a list to persist in **one transaction**. This separation makes each piece independently testable and swappable. The contract details — `read()` returns `null` at end-of-data, `process()` returns `null` to filter, `write()` receives `Chunk<T>` (Spring Batch 5) so a single bulk INSERT replaces N round-trips — are what make chunk steps fast and restart-safe.

sections.title: The Chunk Pipeline Is a Transaction Loop, Not a Stream
sections.content:
**`ItemReader`**, **`ItemProcessor`**, and **`ItemWriter`** are the three roles in Spring Batch's chunk-oriented processing pipeline. What makes the model non-obvious is the **transaction boundary**: read happens outside the commit scope, but the write of all processed items in a chunk happens inside one atomic transaction.

**Per-chunk flow at a glance:**
- Call `ItemReader.read()` until chunk size is reached (or `null` signals end-of-data)
- Pass each item through `ItemProcessor.process()`; collect surviving items
- Call `ItemWriter.write(chunk)` with the entire list in one transaction
- Commit transaction; update `StepExecution` counts; loop

**The contract details that catch candidates:**
- `ItemReader.read()` returns `null` for end-of-data, **not** an exception
- `ItemProcessor.process()` returns `null` to **silently filter** the item out
- `ItemWriter.write(chunk)` receives a list — one call per chunk; bulk INSERT is the point
- Spring Batch 5 changed the writer signature from `write(List<T>)` to `write(Chunk<T>)`; the `Chunk` carries `ChunkContext` for step metadata access

The transaction boundary is also why **write-phase failures are expensive**. If `ItemWriter` fails partway through a chunk, the entire chunk rolls back — Spring Batch then re-reads the chunk one item at a time to isolate the bad row. Every item in the failed chunk is reprocessed; **make processors idempotent** to tolerate this safely.

sections.title: Wiring Reader, Processor, and Writer with @StepScope
Fault Tolerance — Retry, Skip, and Single-Item Recovery
sections.content:
Spring Batch's fault tolerance operates at two levels: **retry** (attempt the same item again) and **skip** (discard the item and continue). Both interact with the transaction boundary in non-obvious ways.

**Retry — for transient failures**
- DB deadlocks (`DeadlockLoserDataAccessException`), network blips, upstream 503s
- `faultTolerant().retry(DeadlockLoserDataAccessException.class).retryLimit(3)`
- Combine with `ExponentialBackOffPolicy` to avoid retry storms

**Skip — for poison records**
- `faultTolerant().skip(ValidationException.class).skipLimit(100)`
- Skipped items are recorded in `StepExecution` for audit; pair with a `SkipListener` that writes to a dead-letter destination

**The single-item recovery cycle (the part candidates miss)**
- When write fails, Spring Batch can't know which item caused it
- It rolls back the chunk transaction
- Then re-reads each item one at a time, processing and writing individually
- The good items succeed; the bad one is skipped (if configured) or fails the step
- This is why **processors must be idempotent** — they may run twice for the same input

```java
.faultTolerant()
    .skip(FlatFileParseException.class)
    .skip(ValidationException.class)
    .skipLimit(500)
    .listener(new SkipListener<Order, Invoice>() {
        @Override public void onSkipInRead(Throwable t) { dlq.send("READ", t); }
        @Override public void onSkipInProcess(Order i, Throwable t) { dlq.send(i, t); }
        @Override public void onSkipInWrite(Invoice i, Throwable t) { dlq.send(i, t); }
    })
    .retry(DeadlockLoserDataAccessException.class)
    .retryLimit(3)
    .backOffPolicy(new ExponentialBackOffPolicy())
```

**Non-transactional side effects under rollback**
- Sending emails, calling external APIs, publishing Kafka events — **rollback does not undo these**
- Move side effects to a final tasklet that runs only after the chunk step completes
- Or use the **outbox pattern** — write a row inside the chunk transaction; a separate step dispatches it

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`ItemReader.read()` returns `null` for end-of-data** — not an exception; throwing is for genuine errors.
- **`ItemProcessor.process()` returns `null` to silently filter** — the item is removed from the chunk and never reaches the writer.
- **`ItemWriter.write(chunk)` receives the entire chunk** — one call; bulk INSERT/UPDATE is the whole point.
- **`@StepScope` is required for parameterized readers/writers** — also makes them safe under concurrent job executions.
- **`CompositeItemProcessor` chains processors** — validate → enrich → transform as composable units.
- **Single-item recovery on write failure** — the chunk re-reads one at a time to isolate the bad row; processors must be idempotent.
- **Readers are not thread-safe by default** — wrap with `SynchronizedItemStreamReader` for multi-threaded steps.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
The chunk-oriented step has three roles, each with a precise contract.

**`ItemReader` — read one item at a time**
- Spring Batch calls `read()` repeatedly until it returns `null`
- `null` is the normal end-of-data signal; throwing is for errors
- Built-in readers: `FlatFileItemReader`, `JdbcCursorItemReader`, `JdbcPagingItemReader`, `JpaPagingItemReader`, `KafkaItemReader`

**`ItemProcessor` — transform or filter one item**
- Receives one item; returns the transformed item or `null` to skip
- `null` silently removes the item from the chunk — never reaches the writer
- Stateless by design; compose with `CompositeItemProcessor`

**`ItemWriter` — write the entire chunk**
- Receives `Chunk<T>` (Spring Batch 5) — all processed items
- Bulk INSERT/UPDATE in one DB call; never loop and write one at a time
- Built-in writers: `JdbcBatchItemWriter`, `JpaItemWriter`, `FlatFileItemWriter`, `KafkaItemWriter`

**Fault tolerance subtlety:**
- Skip on write failure triggers a chunk rollback and single-item replay to isolate the bad row
- Every item in the failed chunk reprocesses — processors must be idempotent
- Non-transactional side effects (emails, API calls) are NOT rolled back; use a final tasklet or outbox pattern

**Thread safety:**
- `FlatFileItemReader` and `JdbcCursorItemReader` maintain cursor state — wrap in `SynchronizedItemStreamReader` for multi-threaded steps
- Paging readers are safer for concurrency since each page is independent

In an interview I'd emphasize the null-return semantics and the single-item retry behaviour — those are what catch candidates.

questions.question: How do you route items to multiple destinations in Spring Batch using `CompositeItemWriter` and `ClassifierCompositeItemWriter`? When does each apply?
questions.title: CompositeItemWriter and ClassifierCompositeItemWriter Patterns
questions.direct_answer: **`CompositeItemWriter`** delegates each chunk to **every** wrapped writer in order — use it when every item must be persisted to multiple sinks (DB plus audit file plus Kafka). **`ClassifierCompositeItemWriter`** uses a `Classifier<T, ItemWriter<? super T>>` to route each item to **exactly one** writer based on a property — use it when items split into categories (valid vs invalid, high-priority vs normal, region A vs region B). Both patterns let you keep the chunk-step transaction model while fan-out or splitting writes; both must implement `ItemStream` correctly so restart and `ExecutionContext` flow through the wrapped writers.

sections.title: Composite Writers Keep the Chunk Model When You Need Fan-Out or Routing
sections.content:
Real batch jobs rarely write to a single destination.
- A typical financial-import job persists records to a primary database, writes an audit copy to a flat file, and publishes events to Kafka.
- A user-import job writes valid users to the user table and invalid rows to a quarantine file for review.
- Both patterns are well served by Spring Batch's composite writers.

**`CompositeItemWriter`** — fan-out semantics. Every wrapped writer receives the entire chunk. Order of delegation matches the order in which writers were registered.

**`ClassifierCompositeItemWriter`** — routing semantics. A `Classifier<T, ItemWriter<? super T>>` examines each item and selects one writer. Items destined for the same writer are batched together and handed off as a sub-chunk.

Both preserve the **chunk-step transaction model** — all writes happen inside the same transaction managed by the step's `PlatformTransactionManager`.
- This is critical: if any write fails, the entire chunk rolls back across all destinations.
- Mixing transaction managers (e.g. one for DB, one for Kafka) breaks atomicity; use the **outbox pattern** instead when you need eventual delivery to non-transactional sinks.

sections.title: CompositeItemWriter — Fan-Out to Multiple Sinks
sections.content:
`CompositeItemWriter` delegates each chunk to every wrapped writer. Use it when **every item** must reach **multiple sinks**.

**Configuration**

```java
@Bean
public CompositeItemWriter<Order> compositeWriter(
        JdbcBatchItemWriter<Order> dbWriter,
        FlatFileItemWriter<Order> auditWriter,
        KafkaItemWriter<String, Order> kafkaWriter) {
    CompositeItemWriter<Order> writer = new CompositeItemWriter<>();
    writer.setDelegates(List.of(dbWriter, auditWriter, kafkaWriter));
    return writer;
}
```

**Delegation behavior**
- Each delegate's `write(chunk)` is called in registration order
- All delegates see the **same chunk**
- If any delegate throws, the chunk is rolled back; remaining delegates are not called

**`ItemStream` propagation**
- `CompositeItemWriter` implements `ItemStream` and delegates `open`, `update`, `close` to wrapped writers that implement `ItemStream`
- `FlatFileItemWriter` saves position in `ExecutionContext` via `update()`
- Without proper `ItemStream` propagation, restart breaks for stateful writers
- This is automatic with `CompositeItemWriter` — but custom composite implementations must do it explicitly

**Transaction model**
- All writes happen inside the step's transaction
- A `JdbcBatchItemWriter` enrolls in the transaction via `DataSourceTransactionManager`
- A `KafkaItemWriter` does NOT enroll in JDBC transactions — Kafka writes commit immediately
- This is the dangerous case: DB rollback does not undo the Kafka publish

**The outbox pattern when atomicity matters**
- Insert a row into an `outbox` table inside the chunk transaction
- A separate dispatcher step (or service) reads outbox rows and publishes to Kafka, marking them dispatched
- Guarantees at-least-once delivery; the DB transaction is the source of truth

**Common fan-out pitfalls**
- **Order of delegates matters for failure semantics** — put the most-likely-to-fail writer first to fail fast
- **Mixing transactional and non-transactional sinks without outbox** — silent inconsistency on rollback
- **Custom writers that loop and call REST APIs** — defeats batching, defeats transaction; use a tasklet or outbox

sections.title: ClassifierCompositeItemWriter — Routing Items by Property
CompositeItemWriter vs ClassifierCompositeItemWriter
sections.content:
Pick the writer pattern that matches the routing intent.

| Aspect | `CompositeItemWriter` | `ClassifierCompositeItemWriter` |
|---|---|---|
| Semantics | Every item to every writer | Each item to one writer |
| Use case | Fan-out (DB + audit + Kafka) | Routing (valid vs invalid, region split) |
| ItemStream propagation | Automatic | Manual via `.stream(writer)` on step |
| Sub-batching | Single chunk to each writer | Sub-chunks per destination, batched |
| Failure | Rollback everything | Rollback everything across destinations |

sections.title: When Composite Writers Help, When They Hurt
sections.content:
**When composite writers help:**
- Multi-destination requirements without leaving the chunk transaction model
- Audit-and-persist patterns common in financial and compliance jobs
- Quarantine flows for invalid records
- Region-based or category-based routing

**When composite writers hurt:**
- Mixing transactional and non-transactional sinks (DB + Kafka) without an outbox — silent inconsistency on rollback
- Routing logic that becomes complex enough to warrant a separate step (extract the classifier as a processor first)
- Per-item small destinations that defeat batching (e.g., 100 destinations with 1 item each)

**Watch for:**
- **Missing `ItemStream` registration** for `ClassifierCompositeItemWriter` delegates — restart silently breaks
- **Mixed transaction managers** — DB rollback does not undo Kafka or REST side effects
- **Custom composite writer that loops over delegates** — easy to forget chunk semantics; use the framework's `CompositeItemWriter`
- **Classifier with side effects** — must be a pure function; expensive classifiers slow down every chunk
- **No idempotency on destinations** — restart re-writes the chunk; non-idempotent writers create duplicates

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`CompositeItemWriter`** — fan-out; every wrapped writer receives the chunk in registration order.
- **`ClassifierCompositeItemWriter`** — routing; each item goes to exactly one writer based on a `Classifier`.
- **All writes share the step's transaction** — rollback affects all destinations.
- **`ItemStream` propagation is automatic for `CompositeItemWriter`** — must be wired manually for `ClassifierCompositeItemWriter` via `.stream(writer)`.
- **Mixing transactional and non-transactional sinks** — DB rollback does not undo Kafka publishes; use the outbox pattern.
- **`BackToBackPatternClassifier`** lets you declaratively map property values to destinations.
- **Idempotency is required** — failed chunks re-execute on restart; destinations must tolerate re-writes (UPSERT, keys).

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
Spring Batch has two composite-writer patterns that cover almost every multi-destination requirement.

**`CompositeItemWriter` — fan-out:**
- Delegates each chunk to every wrapped writer in registration order
- Use when every item must reach multiple sinks (DB plus audit file plus Kafka)
- All writes share the step's transaction — a failure rolls back all destinations
- Implements `ItemStream` and propagates `open`/`update`/`close` to wrapped writers

**`ClassifierCompositeItemWriter` — routing:**
- Uses a `Classifier<T, ItemWriter<? super T>>` to route each item to exactly one writer
- Use when items split into categories — valid vs invalid, region A vs region B
- Items destined for the same writer are batched into sub-chunks, preserving batching
- `ItemStream` does NOT propagate automatically; register destination writers via `.stream(writer)` on the step

**Transaction subtlety:**
- All writers enrolled in the JDBC `PlatformTransactionManager` participate in rollback
- Kafka or REST writers do NOT — they commit immediately
- For atomicity across DB and Kafka, use the outbox pattern: write a row inside the chunk transaction, dispatch from a separate step

**Pattern-matching classifier:**
- `BackToBackPatternClassifier` maps property values (or regex) to destinations declaratively
- Useful for region-based or category-based routing

**Idempotency required:**
- Failed chunks re-execute on restart
- Destinations must tolerate re-writes — UPSERT, idempotency keys, or downstream deduplication

In an interview I'd flag the mixed-transaction-manager pitfall — that's the production bug composite writers most often produce.
